sources.title: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment: Hurricane Maria, September 18, 2017
sources.organization: Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, with technical support from GFDRR, UNDP, EU, UN, OECS and World Bank Group
sources.temporal_coverage: Hurricane Maria effects and recovery needs; figures reported through November 2017.
sources.methodology: Government-led multisector post-disaster assessment of physical, economic, social and sector effects and recovery needs.
sources.limitations: Immediate 2017 recovery estimates; reported damage and projections are not a later recovery evaluation.

sources.title: Dominica: Disaster Resilience Strategy
sources.organization: Government of Dominica; published by the International Monetary Fund
geographic_coverage: towns and communities affected by Hurricane Maria
sources.temporal_coverage: Government disaster-resilience strategy, August 2021; includes the post-Maria emergency and recovery period.
sources.methodology: Government strategy prepared with stakeholder and development-partner consultation and hosted by IMF.
sources.limitations: The strategy summarizes reported post-disaster conditions; it is not a causal study of violence or insecurity.

sources.title: Dominica’s Journey to Become the World’s First Climate Resilient Country
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project outputs and infrastructure works reported in 2023, including the 2022 trough event.
sources.methodology: World Bank project feature summarizing reported disaster-risk-reduction outputs and infrastructure works.
sources.limitations: The feature reports project outputs and works in progress, not an independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Strengthening Community Resilience within Kalinago Territory, Project Document
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica
sources.temporal_coverage: Signed project design for July 2025–December 2026, including cited poverty context and planned activities.
sources.methodology: UNDP project document sets out a local situation analysis, implementation risks, theory of change and planned activities.
sources.limitations: Some poverty and livelihood context cites older sources; intended outputs and social-cohesion outcomes are not measured results.

sources.title: Kalinago Families Receive Tools and Training to Strengthen Food Security and Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP community distribution and training reported in August 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP press release describes project activities, delivered inputs and participating households.
sources.limitations: Implementer reporting of early project outputs; no independent assessment of sustained food-security or resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Update: Government of Dominica Response to Trough System – April 30
sources.organization: Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, Office of the Prime Minister
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood and landslide impacts from the 26 April 2026 trough and immediate response update published 1 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Government response update based on field visits, rapid household assessments and reports from responsible agencies.
sources.limitations: An early operational update; damage, assistance and restoration figures were provisional and evolving.

claims.paraphrase: The PDNA reports about 500 artisans in the Kalinago Territory; around 98% had workspaces damaged or destroyed, and some also lost craft stock. Craft sales were a major Indigenous-community income source.
claims.limitations: PDNA damage estimate from the immediate recovery period; it does not measure longer-term livelihood recovery.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 28–29 (printed), Human and Social Impact and shelter table
claims.paraphrase: As of 8 November 2017, 1,862 people remained in 63 shelters after Maria; 32% were reported among the most vulnerable, including older people, single female-headed households and people with chronic illness.
claims.limitations: Dated shelter snapshot; the report says many displaced people had returned or moved elsewhere by this date.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The PDNA identifies these residents as displaced by Hurricane Maria; it does not attribute displacement to conflict or violence.

claims.locator: PDF p. 17, paragraph 35, post-disaster social resilience
claims.paraphrase: The government strategy says extreme social conditions after Hurricane Maria triggered episodes of looting and social unrest; authorities declared a curfew and deployed security forces, while insufficient property protection slowed recovery businesses.
claims.limitations: The strategy reports limited post-disaster episodes, not armed conflict or a broader trend in violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The government strategy explicitly links extreme post-Maria social conditions with looting and social unrest and says inadequate property protection slowed recovery.

claims.locator: PDF p. 17, paragraphs 33–34, post-disaster preparedness and recovery
claims.paraphrase: The strategy says damaged feeder roads isolated some communities and missing population, socioeconomic and location data limited response targeting; needs handled through direct requests to Cabinet and Finance created inefficiencies and possible duplicate benefits.
claims.limitations: The strategy describes emergency-response constraints after Maria; it does not attribute them to conflict or insecurity.

claims.locator: WB feature section on disaster-risk data systems, paragraphs on hydromet monitoring
claims.paraphrase: DVRP expanded hydromet monitoring from two airports to 44 stations, gauges and water-level sensors islandwide. In November 2022 the network measured 500 mm of rain in the Southeast over two days.
claims.limitations: Project reporting; data-system output, not forecast accuracy or avoided losses.

claims.locator: WB feature paragraphs on western-coast water tanks, printed article section 2
claims.paraphrase: Eight western-coast tanks built in 2020 serve 20 communities and 11,000 people, adding over 1 million litres of storage; water-system sections and access roads were also upgraded after Maria.
claims.limitations: Reported construction and reach; later service continuity was not independently assessed.

claims.locator: WB feature paragraphs on East Coast Road and access to Indigenous communities
claims.paraphrase: DVRP’s 31-km East Coast Road works include slope/landslide stabilization, flood mitigation and bridge/culvert works; the route carries farm produce and connects the Kalinago community to services and tourist sites.
claims.scenario: Road works under construction in 2023; completion is not verified.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 3–5, Kalinago Territory context and vulnerability analysis
claims.paraphrase: The project document describes eight Kalinago hamlets under communal land governance; it cites a 2015 poverty assessment finding 50% of residents poor and notes reliance on agriculture and forest products vulnerable to ecosystem degradation and climate hazards.
claims.limitations: The 50% poverty statistic is cited from a 2015 government assessment, not re-estimated in this project document.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 5, 8 and 11, prior project land-tenure issue, community participation and theory of change
claims.paraphrase: The project identifies communal-land compensation contention and political instability as risks; it plans a Council-controlled greenhouse site and community-led activities, with stronger Kalinago social cohesion an intended long-term outcome.
claims.scenario: UNDP project design for 2025–2026; risks and social-cohesion benefits are prospective, not evaluated results.
claims.limitations: The design documents project rationale and anticipated impact; it does not document actual violence or measured cohesion change.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The theory of change names political instability as a potential risk and social cohesion as an intended outcome; neither is evidence of actual conflict or demonstrated peace effects.

claims.locator: UNDP release paragraphs 2–6, 36 households and backyard-gardening support, August 2026
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports 36 Kalinago Territory households received seedlings, fruit trees, tools, tarpaulins, water-storage equipment and climate-smart agriculture training through SCR-K; delivery was coordinated with the Kalinago Council and IsraAID Dominica.
claims.limitations: Implementer reports early outputs; further supplies were pending and longer-term food-security effects were not assessed.

claims.locator: Government update paragraphs 5–11, 26 April 2026 trough impacts and recovery actions
claims.paraphrase: After a trough caused flooding and landslides, the government reported impacts in Antrizzle, Atkinson, the Kalinago Territory and Castle Bruce, including low-pressure water service, blocked farm access and crop/livestock losses; water and road restoration and farm inputs were under way.
claims.limitations: The May 2026 update is an early government operational account; restoration and assistance were ongoing.

claims.locator: Government update paragraphs 9–10, rapid household assessment and social relief in Atkinson and Antrizzle
claims.paraphrase: Rapid assessments identified 22 affected households comprising 64 people in Atkinson and Antrizzle; food packages were distributed with DEXIA and the Red Cross, and psychosocial support was provided.
claims.limitations: Government rapid-assessment and relief figures are preliminary and cover only the named communities in this update.

search_audit.query: Dominica Kalinago Territory local climate vulnerability poverty agriculture landslides water
search_audit.outcome: The government PDNA and UNDP project document identify Kalinago livelihood and social vulnerabilities; the May 2026 government update and World Bank feature add named East Coast and Southeast exposures.

search_audit.query: Dominica Hurricane Maria displacement looting social unrest climate disaster livelihood loss official report
search_audit.outcome: The PDNA attributes shelter displacement to Maria; the government strategy reports post-Maria looting and social unrest and identifies recovery and civil-security constraints. No source inspected establishes armed conflict or climate-caused conflict.

search_audit.query: Dominica insecurity political instability conflict constrains climate adaptation disaster response official source
search_audit.outcome: The UNDP project theory of change lists political instability as a possible implementation risk; the government strategy describes weak post-disaster response information and property protection. No inspected source documents actual conflict or insecurity obstructing adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Dominica community climate resilience disaster risk management capacity local adaptation official report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank reports expanded hydromet data, water storage and East Coast Road risk-reduction works; UNDP documents Kalinago household inputs and training; the government reports immediate 2026 flood/landslide response. Planned infrastructure and early response are distinguished from evaluated outcomes.

gaps: No inspected source attributes armed conflict or sustained political violence in Dominica to climate hazards. The government strategy does report limited post-Maria looting and social unrest, without characterizing it as armed conflict.

The first Biennial Transparency Report PDF was returned as a timeout and the Green Climate Fund adaptation-planning page as access denied; neither was used for claims. The UN human-security country assessment PDF was also inaccessible and not used.
The UNDP project document cites older poverty context and presents social cohesion and resilience gains as prospective; these are not evaluated outcomes.

No source inspected documents actual conflict or insecurity blocking climate-adaptation delivery; political instability appears only as a prospective project risk, while immediate recovery constraints are documented separately.
